subscriptionTag: Maurizio Cattelan - Novecento by Maurizio Cattelan
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition of Maurizio Cattelan’s Novecento, the legendary suspended taxidermy horse, created in 1997 and now available as an edition for the first time.
description:
As Maurizio Cattelan’s Novecento enters its 30th-anniversary year, the legendary sculpture becomes a limited edition for the first time.

Originally created in 1997, Novecento is a taxidermy horse suspended from the ceiling by a leather harness and metal cables. The sculpture was prominently featured in Cattelan’s seminal retrospective, Maurizio Cattelan: All, at the Guggenheim Museum in New York in 2011-12. Named after the Italian word for the 20th century, the artwork invokes an era defined by extraordinary technological ambition and the devastation of two World Wars – setting the stage for the work’s power struggle between grandeur, power, audacity and death.

This edition has been designed to hang from the ceiling using an adjustable twine cord, stylistically based on the original artwork, installed via a metal bracket. Each sculpture is hand-painted, individually numbered and accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity, with a hanging guide included for installation. This edition is paired with Not Afraid of Love, and part of a wider series of sculpture editions, including We Are the Revolution and La Nona Ora.
authentication: Hand-written edition number. Each edition is accompanied by a certificate of authenticity, signed by Maurizio Cattelan.
mediumDescription: Individually hand-painted resin sculpture, with adjustable twine hanging attachment.

subscriptionTag: Robert Longo - Untitled (Sandy from Men in the Cities) by Robert Longo
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition silkscreen print by Robert Longo in support of Vote.org. Drawn from the celebrated and rarely editioned Men in the Cities, Untitled (Sandy) is one of the series’ best-known figures.

Released in support of Vote.org, Robert Longo’s new limited edition silkscreen print explores power, politics and the human condition.

Untitled (Sandy) is one of the rarest and best-known figures from Longo’s Men in the Cities series, a collection of graphite and charcoal drawings based on photographs of the artist’s friends and contemporaries taken on the roof of his New York studio in the late 70s and early 80s. Longo used ropes, loud noises and threw objects at his models to achieve the surreal half dancing, half dying movements of his reference imagery – which was partially inspired by the final scenes of Fassbinder’s film The American Soldier (1970).

Sandy has been deliberately produced at the same scale and dimensions as Eric for repeat collectors who may wish to display the two pieces together.

Our master printmakers have used Longo’s original Kodak transparencies to craft this limited edition print, resulting in a high level of fidelity with the original charcoal drawing.
authentication: Signed by the artist. Individually numbered.

subscriptionTag: Maurizio Cattelan - Novecento by Maurizio Cattelan
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition of Maurizio Cattelan’s Not Afraid of Love, the celebrated elephant sculpture created in 2000 and now available as an edition for the first time.
description:
Ten years after Not Afraid of Love marked Maurizio Cattelan’s triumphant return to the art world, the sculpture that gave the exhibition its name is editioned for the first time.

Originally created in 2000, Not Afraid of Love depicts a giant elephant concealed beneath a white sheet with two eye-holes. In 2016, the work lent its title to Cattelan’s major exhibition at the Monnaie de Paris, five years after he boldly announced his retirement from the art world following his 2011 retrospective at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum. Playing on the expression “elephant in the room”, the work turns an imposing creature into an absurd and vulnerable figure in hiding – a characteristically on-the-nose joke that, with disarming simplicity, opens onto a near-endless range of interpretations.

Each sculpture is hand-painted, individually numbered and accompanied by a Certificate of Authenticity. This edition is paired with Novecento, and part of a wider series of sculpture editions, including We Are the Revolution and La Nona Ora
authentication: Hand-written edition number. Each edition is accompanied by a certificate of authenticity, signed by Maurizio Cattelan.

subscriptionTag: Bisa Butler - I Go To Prepare A Place For You by Bisa Butler
seoDescription: Collect Bisa Butler’s I Go To Prepare A Place For You, a limited-edition print depicting Harriet Tubman, created as a fundraising edition for Smithsonian American Art Museum and Renwick Gallery and National Museum of African American History and Culture
description:
Bisa Butler brings a powerful portrait from American history to a new limited-edition print, created as a fundraising edition for Smithsonian American Art Museum and Renwick Gallery and National Museum of African American History and Culture

I Go To Prepare A Place For You, created in 2021, is a quilted and appliquéd textile portrait based on a 19th-century photograph of abolitionist Harriet Tubman by Benjamin F. Powelson. In the artwork, Butler uses a palette of blues to reflect Tubman's life in hiding as she carried out her work as a social activist, set against passages of red that speak to her strength, determination and unwavering will to be free. As Tubman herself once said: "There are two things I've got a right to, and these are Death, or Liberty – one or the other I mean to have."

Butler’s original work is held in the collection of the National Museum of African American History and Culture, Washington DC. This edition brings the artwork into print for the first time, with proceeds supporting Smithsonian American Art Museum and Renwick Gallery and National Museum of African American History and Culture.

description:

Hemisphere takes its name from the brain's two hemispheres, using this as a metaphor for the shifting relationship between Islamic tradition and contemporary cultural identity. The work presents a central dome split into two halves: one side in the green of the Prophet Muhammad's Mosque in Medina, representing the peaceful heart of Islam, and the other modelled on an ancient warrior's helmet, representing how religion can be misinterpreted for political ends.

Gharem first created the composition as a painting in 2013, using a stamp technique inspired by traditional Islamic interior design, before reimagining it as a sculpture in 2017. The painting has been exhibited worldwide, with major exhibitions at LACMA and the Station Museum of Modern Art. The painting and sculpture have also been exhibited together at the Sharjah Art Museum.

subscriptionTag: Johnson Tsang - Alliance by Johnson Tsang
seoDescription: Collect a new limited edition sculpture by Johnson Tsang exploring coexistence, intimacy and human connection through six intertwined cherubic faces rendered in the artist’s signature hyperreal sculptural style.
description:
Johnson Tsang's new limited edition sculpture asks what it really means to live alongside others.

Alliance depicts a line of six cherubic baby faces, smooshed cheek-to-cheek in tender, almost suffocating closeness – capturing what Tsang describes as "the entangled, love-hate relationship between people". description:
The seminal series Homage to the Square by Josef Albers becomes a new silkscreen print.

One of the most influential artists of the 20th century, Josef began his practice at the Bauhaus art school in Berlin, where he became a key figure in its visual culture. Forced to flee Nazi Germany in 1933, he and his wife Anni emigrated to the United States, where their work helped reshape the language of modern art. As a professor at Yale, Josef became a pioneering figure in colour theory, with his painting practice shaped by his seminal book Interaction of Color.

Produced in close collaboration with the Josef and Anni Albers Foundation, this fundraising edition has been made with the greatest care to honour the precision and chromatic clarity that define his legacy. The release fundraises for  Bët-bi – a new museum, culture and community centre in Senegal, developed by the Josef and Anni Albers Foundation and Le Korsa.

This reproduction of Homage to the Square, (Red) is authorised by, and has been produced under license from, The Josef and Anni Albers Foundation and is part of a finite edition of 250 authorised reproductions.

subscriptionTag: Ai Weiwei - Self-Portrait Embroidery (Purple & Yellow), Self-Portrait Embroidery (Blue & Pink) by Ai Weiwei
seoDescription: Discover Ai Weiwei’s landmark self-portrait reimagined as a pair of limited edition embroideries, each translating his defiant spirit, political conviction, and toy-brick aesthetic into richly textured textile works.
description:
Ai Weiwei transforms a defiant self-portrait into a new limited edition pair of embroideries.

In 2011, following 81 days in detention with Chinese authorities, Weiwei and his team secretly created toy brick portraits of global political prisoners for a major show at the decommissioned Alcatraz prison in San Francisco. Due to his passport being confiscated, Weiwei was unable to attend the exhibition, uniting him in solidarity with his subjects.

Presented here as a pair, the pixelated embroidery translates a self-portrait of Weiwei with a shaved head and scar – the result of police brutality following his investigation into the 2008 Sichuan earthquake, which caused the artist to haemorrhage. It forms a powerful statement of persistence and solidarity, reflecting Weiwei’s unwavering belief that “it is your duty as an artist to fight and to protect freedom of speech.”

Both individual embroideries in the pair feature approximately 460,000 stitches, embroidered in 5 colours on 230gsm cotton and mounted in a bespoke frame. Each is meticulously crafted to translate the pixelated texture and bold presence of the original toy brick work.

seoDescription: Discover Man Ray's haunting Surrealist portrait as a limited edition print. The iconic 1932 image features a model crying tears of glistening glass beads, exemplifying his radical emotive approach.
description:
An iconic Surrealist portrait by Man Ray becomes a new limited edition print, in collaboration with his Estate.

This edition is based on Larmes (Tears), originally photographed around 1932 during Man Ray's time in Paris. The haunting image shows a model gazing upward, crying tears of glistening glass beads. Created around the time of Man Ray's breakup with photographer Lee Miller, the work exemplifies his radical and emotive approach to photography that helped shape both Dada and Surrealism. Man Ray considered this one of his most successful photographs, featuring it prominently in his 1934 photographic book.

This limited edition print features a matte varnish seal and bespoke debossed archive stamp, carefully crafted by our expert printmakers at our London fine art print studio, Make-Ready.

subscriptionTag: William Blake - Night the Third by William Blake
seoDescription: Collect a new limited edition print that revives a rare book illustration by Romantic master William Blake in collaboration with Sir John Soane’s Museum.
description:
Drawn from the extraordinary collection of Sir John Soane’s Museum, London, this new limited edition print revives a rare book illustration by the forefather of British Romanticism, William Blake.

Night the Third is part of a triptych of limited edition prints based on Blake's illustrated title pages for Edward Young's celebrated 18th-century poem, The Complaint, and the Consolation. While he created over 500 watercolour designs for the project, only 43 were engraved for the 1797 edition. Now, just 28 hand-coloured copies are known to exist, including a copy held at Sir John Soane's Museum. These detailed pieces are considered defining masterpieces of Blake's early work.

Each edition is authenticated with a debossed Museum stamp and accompanied by a certificate of authenticity signed by Will Gompertz, Deborah Loeb Brice Director, Sir John Soane’s Museum.

By collecting this work, supporters directly contribute to Sir John Soane's Museum – the architect's former London home, where his collection remains displayed exactly as he left it on his death in 1837.
authentication:
Authenticated with a debossed museum stamp.
Each edition is accompanied by a certificate of authenticity, signed by Museum Director Will Gompertz.

subscriptionTag: William Blake - Night the First by William Blake
seoDescription: Collect a new limited edition print that revives a rare book illustration by Romantic master William Blake in collaboration with Sir John Soane’s Museum.
description:
Drawn from the extraordinary collection of Sir John Soane's Museum, London, this new limited edition print revives a rare book illustration by the forefather of British Romanticism, William Blake.

Night the First is part of a triptych of limited edition prints based on Blake's illustrated title pages for Edward Young's celebrated 18th-century poem, The Complaint, and the Consolation. While he created over 500 watercolour designs for the project, only 43 were engraved for the 1797 edition. Now, just 28 hand-coloured copies are known to exist, including a copy held at Sir John Soane's Museum. These detailed pieces are considered defining masterpieces of Blake's early work.

Each edition is authenticated with a debossed Museum stamp and accompanied by a certificate of authenticity signed by Will Gompertz, Deborah Loeb Brice Director, Sir John Soane’s Museum.

By collecting this work, supporters directly contribute to Sir John Soane's Museum – the architect's former London home, where his collection remains displayed exactly as he left it on his death in 1837.

A new sculpture by Johnson Tsang holds a powerful personal story of recovery.

Work in Progress is a limited edition sculpture depicting a face emerging from wet clay, still being shaped by unseen hands. seoDescription: Collect a bespoke textured print by Korean artist Kukwon Woo, based on the historic series A Tour of Waterfalls in the Provinces (1833-1834) by Japanese master Hokusai.
description:
Kukwon Woo channels the sacred spirit of Japanese waterfalls in a new multi-layered print.

Waterfall (Rōben) is one of several 2025 waterfall paintings by the Korean artist, fusing inspiration from Hokusai’s historic series, A Tour of Waterfalls in the Provinces (1833-1834), with quotes from the Bible. In this particular work, Woo inscribes a passage from Psalm 42: "Deep calls to deep in the roar of your waterfalls; all your waves and breakers have swept over me." The juxtaposition of the Japanese master’s Ukiyo-e style with Christian scripture creates what the artist describes as an "ironic narrative",  where familiar Eastern imagery becomes a vessel for cross-cultural spirituality.

This richly textured, 13-layer archival pigment print honours the delicate beauty of traditional Japanese woodblock printmaking as well as Woo's contemporary conceptual vision.

Inspired by the work of Edward Hopper and William Eggleston, this piece captures the quietly transcendent magic of everyday city life.

description:
A special edition produced to mark the 75th anniversary of the ICA. All sales proceeds will go towards supporting ICA's future events, exhibitions and learning programme.

XXX, is taken from a painting of the same title, first shown in the artist’s 2019 solo show at White Cube, Hong Kong. The print takes the form of the cover of a novel, with the top section a complex graphic layering of letters and colours, counterbalanced by a clean band of neutral colour bearing the title and author/artist’s name, where drips of paint at the bottom of the canvas expose its layering of colours. The work is part of an ongoing series, where Miller employs mono or bi-syllabic words to create hard-edged letter paintings with bold, saturated colours that reference, amongst others, Robert Rauschenberg and Ed Ruscha’s use of vernacular signage and motifs. Miller depicts the letters in a range of typefaces, through a process of isolating, overlaying and reconnecting, to create a sense of depth in the image that deconstructs and abstracts the meaning of language itself. Inspired by illuminated manuscripts, these works bring a Pop sensibility to the lettering of medieval monks, connecting the sacred with the everyday.

The letter X is significant to the artist in its form and design but also given its connotations and connection to punk culture and X-rated cinema. The letters XXX are built up from layers of various colours, their image suggesting objects in motion, where several forms are compressed at once, kaleidoscopic and transparent – like a series of sequential, transparent slides.

description:
Glenn Brown weaves a tapestry of references in this new limited edition print.

Renowned for transforming art historical and pop cultural imagery into obsessively detailed, often grotesque paintings, the British artist produces only a handful of works each year. For this edition, he reimagines his original oil painting Black Ships Ate the Sky (2020), itself based on two 16th-century portraits: Andrea del Sarto’s Head of a Man in Profile Looking Up and an unknown artist’s (Circle of Carlo Maratta) portrait of Alexander the Great.

In Higher Than the Sun, Brown subtly distorts colour and proportion from Black Ships Ate the Sky, while introducing a bold black bar at the image’s base – homage to a vintage Star Wars poster. Created in close collaboration with our master printmakers at Make-Ready, the edition has been meticulously crafted as a wholly new creation in its own right.

subscriptionTag: Judy Chicago - 'Reincarnation Triptych' - by Judy Chicago
seoDescription: Collect a new limited edition silkscreen print by Judy Chicago. 'Reincarnation Triptych' unites three iconic works in one edition.
description:
Judy Chicago shares the first-ever limited edition print of her legendary Reincarnation Triptych.

Reincarnation Triptych was originally created in 1973 at the height of the women's liberation movement, part of a series of abstract portraits of important historic women, entitled Great Ladies. Uniting three of her most famous works from the series in one piece for the first time, the artist interprets three literary figures: 19th-century philosopher Madame de Staël, French novelist George Sand and modernist writer Virginia Woolf. Each panel features exactly forty words describing the woman represented, written in the Palmer method, a mode of handwriting which the artist learnt as a child. The work epitomises the artist's signature iconography, with its nuanced colour gradients and hypnotising concentric forms.

This 24-colour silkscreen edition has been hand-crafted at our fine art printmaking studio, Make-Ready. It is finished with matte, satin and sparkle gloss varnish – capturing the ethereal quality of Judy's original work.

seoDescription: Ai Weiwei releases a highly anticipated vase sculpture trio, blending ancient craft and modern-day iconography, produced in brass with our artists' metal partners.
description:
This new limited edition vase sculpture sees Ai Weiwei reimagine one of his most iconic mediums.

Weiwei has long engaged with ancient Chinese pottery as a means of cultural and political critique – most famously in his 1995 work Dropping a Han Dynasty Urn, in which he let a 2,000-year-old ceremonial vase crash to the floor. Since then, the object has become a prominent and recurring medium in the artist's prolific oeuvre, from branding ancient pots with consumerist symbols like the Coca-Cola  logo, to dripping Neolithic objects in household paint. Coloured Vase (Green, Blue and Red) continues Weiwei's rich ceramic legacy, blending ancient craft and modern-day iconography to question how cultural value is both constructed and commodified.

Each sculpture edition is produced using a highly skilled metal spinning process. This is our second vase edition with Ai Weiwei, following Glass Vase released in 2023.

Tomokazu Matsuyama reflects on modern life in a vivid ode to American realist Edward Hopper.

Morning Sun Dance, painted in 2025, is the centrepiece of Matsuyama’s current exhibition at Edward Hopper House. Inspired by Hopper’s renowned use of light, Matsuyama created the piece in his own New York studio. Through his distinctive fusion of Japanese and Western artistic styles and motifs, he reflects on the timeless experience of urban solitude.

seoDescription: German artist Katharina Grosse translates her explosive spray-painted landscapes into a new limited edition print, its electric, fast-flowing streaks at once automatic, instinctive and magnetically compelling.
description:
Katharina Grosse translates her explosive spray-painted landscapes into a new limited edition print.

subscriptionTag: Carrie Mae Weems - Untitled (Man & Mirror), Kitchen Table Series by Carrie Mae Weems
seoDescription: Carrie Mae Weems shares her historic Kitchen Table Series with a limited edition photographic print – 35 years on from her landmark photographic series that changed the history of art.
description:
Carrie Mae Weems opens her historic Kitchen Table Series with a staged photograph of love and desire.

In 1990, Carrie Mae Weems took 20 black-and-white images at her kitchen table, a traditionally female space that has not been celebrated enough in art. The overhead bulb sets the stage in each photograph, where a host of intimate domestic scenes and social dynamics unfold.

In Untitled (Man & Mirror), Carrie looks directly into the lens as her lover’s body embraces her from above. In an accompanying text from the original installation, the artist writes: "A thin line of difference was beginning to show itself, but they didn't want to lose this dream, so kept at it. Plus the loving was worth it."

Seamlessly threading together the personal and political, this limited edition print is a testament to the artist's monumental legacy.

Judy Chicago revisits two historic paintings from her early feminist era with a pair of limited edition prints.

Heaven is For White Men Only & Let It All Hang Out, both originally painted in 1973, mark a monumental shift in Judy's practice where she began openly expressing that she was a woman after nearly a decade of trying to hide her gender.

description:
Three works from Lee Ufan's iconic From Point and From Line series are translated to a trio of new limited edition silkscreen prints. They launch in collaboration with Dia Art Foundation, for which the release fundraises.

Born in South Korea in 1936, Lee Ufan is one of contemporary art’s most influential figures. After founding the Mono-ha movement in Japan, he helped lead Dansaekhwa (Korean monochrome painting), where art is reduced to its essential gestures and materials. His renowned From Point and From Line series are influenced by his calligraphy training as a child – the meditative repetition of lines and dots requiring complete command of mind, body, brush and breathing.

Here, the printmakers at Make-Ready have rendered the contemplated gestures of the originals with the upmost care, consideration and quality – from the stains of linseed oil on the canvas to the fading brush marks forever suspended in time – echoing the artist’s own reverence for mark-making.

subscriptionTag: Yoon Hyup - Summer in San Sebastian by Yoon Hyup
seoDescription: Collect a new limited edition print from Brooklyn-based artist Yoon Hyup.
description:
Bask in the warmth of a Summer in San Sebastian by Yoon Hyup.

In 2016, Brooklyn-based artist Yoon Hyup was living in a modest apartment with very little light. Caught in the grasp of fast-paced city life, he found himself yearning for sunlight and nature. So when he was invited to the Spanish city of San Sebastián for the summer, his art practice soon began to reflect his new environment.

Summer in San Sebastian is a painting of the city view from his window, depicted in his signature melody of lines and dots. Over time, this work has become a personal reminder to the artist to slow down, reflect and appreciate the moment.

For this limited edition print, the painting was carefully replicated by our master printers in close collaboration with Yoon, with each colour grade precisely matched to the original painting. The sea, beach and sky are smooth and flat, while the city elements are raised to create a contrasting sculpted effect.

seoDescription: Feel the fast intensity of Chromadynamica 19, a new limited print edition from Argentine-Spanish artist Felipe Pantone. “I think we’re living in times of rapid transformation, driven by technology and the digital age. This piece is a way for me to reflect on and reference that.”
description:
Our latest collaboration with Felipe Pantone transforms a key piece from his defining Chromadynamica series into a new limited edition print.

Chromadynamica 19 P sets colour gradients in motion, taking its name from ancient Greek derivatives for the words ‘colour’ and ‘dynamics’. The pixelated composition references the fast-paced, ever-shifting nature of our digital world, suggesting that change is the only constant thing we have.

Felipe originally created the piece with a Dibond structure, masking tape and enamel spray paint. The process of translating it into an archival pigment print was meticulous, with the artist working alongside our master printmakers to precisely translate the colour grading. The resulting print edition not only remains true to what the artist calls the "vibrant intensity" of the original artwork, but it also takes on a new, powerful life of its own.

subscriptionTag: Cindy Sherman - Untitled by Cindy Sherman

This trio of limited edition prints was originally shot on an expired roll of experimental Polaroid slide film. It is laid out like a projector strip from an old-fashioned cinema, emphasising the poignant and familiar tale of faded Hollywood dreams.

Until now, Untitled has never been released because Sherman deemed these portraits “more pretty” than the rest of the series. Twenty-five years later, the artist shares this hidden gem from her personal archive, launching in support of the Museum of Cycladic Art.

The process of translating it into an archival pigment print was meticulous, with the artist working alongside our master printmakers to precisely translate the colour grading. The resulting print edition not only remains true to what the artist calls the "vibrant intensity" of the original artwork, but it also takes on a new, powerful life of its own.

subscriptionTag: Miwa Komatsu - Innocent Days and Wishes by Miwa Komatsu

Each print is accompanied by The Great Harmonisation — an illustrated poetry book that introduces the conceptual framework of Miwa’s work.

subscriptionTag: Mickalene Thomas - Resist by Mickalene Thomas

description:
Mickalene Thomas presents a rousing portrait of race in the USA.

Originally created in 2017, Resist spans nearly a century of African American history. Mickalene appropriates photojournalistic imagery that centres on moments of racist violence such as the Tulsa Race Massacre (1921), and police dogs attacking a civil rights protestor in Birmingham Alabama (1963). Alongside the brutality she interjects symbols of Black resistance, like protestors bearing ‘freedom’ placards and a portrait of writer and activist James Baldwin. With Resist, Mickalene connects her work to this lineage of freedom fighters.

Mickalene’s technique of overlapping photographs lends itself to the medium of silkscreen printing. As a print, Resist also asks us to consider how news and histories are disseminated. This edition extends that call beyond the confines of a single work, taking Mickalene’s overtly political message to homes around the world.

His army of ‘fiends’ hurl across the sky on horseback, weapons raised for destruction. A chariot carrying the crowned figure is pulled into the centre of the scene by dogs – a nod to the animalistic nature of war. As the sun rises, meteors rain down on the terrifying procession, hinting at the presence of a higher power. Meanwhile, the fire-scorched earth below is a reminder of the devastation that arrives with warfare.

The print edition is finished with glow-in-the-dark silkscreen details, allowing another dimension of the scene to come alive at night.

subscriptionTag: Mickalene Thomas - Landscape With Woman Washing Her Feet by Mickalene Thomas

description:
A figure is lost to history in a rare landscape work by Mickalene Thomas.

In Landscape With Woman Washing Her Feet, Mickalene brings her voice to Nicolas Poussin’s eponymous painting from 1650. The artist became enamoured by the romantic style of the Hudson River School painters after frequent travels to upstate New York in 2008. Using photographs taken during this time, she pieces together the idyllic scene – but the titular woman is absent. A flash of glittering animal print offers a clue at who she might have been.

Landscape With Woman Washing Her Feet shows Mickalene experimenting outside of the bounds of her usual practice. She challenges both the expectations of black art and of landscape painting – using unexpected materials like rhinestones to blur the lines between nature and artifice. Printmakers utilised metallic shimmers, and gloss detailing to replicate the dynamic light and textures of the original.

subscriptionTag: Mickalene Thomas - November 1981 & Afro Goddess Looking Forward by Mickalene Thomas

Notions of self-love and desire play out in two collaged portraits by Mickalene Thomas.

In November 1981, Mickalene Thomas blends playfulness with social commentary on the performance of Black femme desire. The central image is cut out of Jet – an African American magazine founded in 1951. As the Afro Goddess, Mickalene reclines on a couch haloed by her sparkling afro. The portrait centres on the unwavering gaze of the artist’s eyes – cut and pasted from a black and white self-portrait.

subscriptionTag: Robert Longo - Untitled (Eric, from the series “Men in the Cities”) by Robert Longo
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition silkscreen print by Robert Longo from his iconic ‘Men in the Cities’ series, depicting a paradox between dancing and dying.
description:
Punk rock dance meets film noir violence, in Robert Longo's snapshot of 80s New York.

Untitled (Eric) revisits an iconic series that has spawned countless pop culture copycats. In the late 70s and early 80s, "Men in the Cities" took the art world by storm. The images of contorted bodies, suspended between pain and pleasure, became emblematic of the Pictures Generation and marked a new era in image-making.

The transposition of medium is central to the artist's practice. Robert constructs his drawings with layer upon layer of black graphite, working his way from light to dark to give new meaning to his original photographs. Similarly, the intricate process behind the print edition involves layers of grayscale separation. This high level of fidelity with the image, unique to silkscreen, results in a floating effect and hyperreal grain texture.

subscriptionTag: Robert Longo - Untitled (Falling Flag) by Robert Longo
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition silkscreen print by Robert Longo which explores democracy and power through the emblematic American flag.
description:
Robert Longo drops the curtain on the American dream.

The stars and stripes of the American flag have appeared in Robert’s work throughout his career, taking on different meanings with each iteration. This new edition is taken from his recent exploration of democracy and power. For Robert, Untitled (Falling Flag) is about “revealing a void – it’s a curtain falling, and nothing exists beyond.”

The flag itself takes up less than half of the image. The rest of the print is an intense black that represents the imposing “void”. To achieve this solid colour in his original drawing, Robert built up layer upon layer of charcoal on white paper. This process is mirrored in the silkscreen process, which included grayscale separation across 9 colours. This allows the complexity of the dark charcoal in Robert’s original to come to life with a hyper-realistic grain texture.

subscriptionTag: Shirin Neshat  - Unveiling series #1, 1993 & Unveiling series #2, 1993 & Women Without Men #1, 2009 & Women Without Men #2, 2009 by Shirin Neshat
seoDescription: Purchase a collection of limited edition prints by artist Shirin Neshat
description:
Collect a quartet of limited edition prints drawing on seminal works from Shirin Neshat’s career.

The collection comprises two photographic prints, based on stills from Shirin’s internationally-acclaimed film Women Without Men. Two signature calligraphy and photography pieces, each with a separate silkscreen layer of handwritten Farsi by the artist, complete the set.

Living in exile since the Islamic Republic of Iran’s seizing of power in 1979, Shirin has unwaveringly shaped global conversation of gender and identity, focusing her lens on where the personal meets the political.
releaseNote: Unveiling series #1, 1993: Edition of 255 / Unveiling series #2, 1993: Edition of 161 / Women Without Men #1, 2009: Edition of 118 / Women Without Men #2, 2009: Edition of 116

seoDescription: Collect an uplifting new limited edition silkscreen print by LY, signalling a new chapter in her exploration of colour.
description:
In this new limited edition silkscreen print, LY brings bright hope for the future.

In 2023, LY introduced her amorphous, wandering muse, LUV, to a world of colour – breaking free from the monochromatic legacy that once defined her practice. Here, she guides the character into a golden-hued forest – its trees symbolising growth and limitless potential.

To bring LY’s first exploration of this new palette to life, printmakers at Make-Ready meticulously translated each carefully chosen shade into a complex, 20-colour silkscreen. The result is a vivacious celebration of colour, marking a joyful new chapter in the artist’s practice.

subscriptionTag: Ayako Rokkaku - Untitled by Ayako Rokkaku
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition silkscreen print by Japanese artist Ayako Rokkaku.
description:
A wide-eyed child drifts through the vast unknown in a new limited edition silkscreen print by Ayako Rokkaku.

Ayako pursues an ‘instinctive, primal impulse’ by painting with her fingertips. Like a child at play, she abandons brushes, applying acrylic paint spontaneously with her hands. Intuitive emotion becomes rich swathes of colour, from which a character begins to appear.

In our second collaboration, a blonde, long-limbed girl emerges through kaleidoscopic clouds. Clutching a life-sized pink toy, she embodies the kawaii-inspired fictional characters that shaped Ayako's childhood in Japan. While the vibrant scene exudes ‘positive energy’, the child’s ambiguous expression invites reflection on the complexities of childhood.

subscriptionTag: Hajime Sorayama - Untitled by Hajime Sorayama
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition lenticular print by Japanese artist Hajime Sorayama.
description:
In this new lenticular limited edition, one of the legendary Japanese artist's gynoids breathes 3D life.

Sorayama’s decade-spanning series of 'sexy robots' have influenced everyone from fashion designers to global pop icons. Here, one of the figures – a symbol of the artist’s "strong desire to depict the goddess" – takes centre stage in a piece that gives the illusion of depth and movement as you move around it.

Sorayama is in constant pursuit of light. Specifically, “the way that metal absorbs and reflects light.” Offering immersion in his inimitable visual universe, this edition sees that pursuit taken to new places.

subscriptionTag: Jammie Holmes - Fred by Jammie Holmes
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by American painter Jammie Holmes that honours the legacy of activist Fred Hampton.
description:
In Fred, Jammie Holmes places childhood memories in the context of the Black liberation struggle.

Jammie’s practice centres the spaces where Black life is lived in the Deep South. Fred, offers a window into such a space — a family living room with checkered floors and wood panelled walls. The TV screen is a black and white portrait of Fred Hampton — deputy chairman of the Black Panther Party who was assassinated in 1969 at the age of 21. Above the television is a photograph from Jammie’s childhood framed with gold leaf, and the handles on its 80s style cabinet are printed in metallic ink. The whole scene is lined with gold glitter, framing the memory as precious.

A rotating sequence of flags form an imposing border around the print. Jammie incorporates (from top left): the 13 Stripes representing the 13th amendment that abolished slavery, the tricolour Pan-African flag, the African American Flag (1990) by artist David Hammonds, and a flag of Jammie’s own creation. The flags represent the past, present and future of Black liberation in the US.

subscriptionTag: Tomás Sánchez - El testigo & Cascada como ícono by Tomás Sánchez
seoDescription: 'Cascada como ícono' is a UV pigment print on 410gsm Somerset Tub Sized Radiant White paper. 'El testigo' is a UV pigment print on 410gsm Somerset Tub Sized Radiant White paper with a matte varnish seal.
description:
Tomás Sánchez captures the transcendent power of golden hour in a pair of luminous new prints.

In El Testigo, towering treetops form arches “reminiscent of temples". In Cascada como ícono, a cascading waterfall becomes a portal for reflection.

To create the editions, printers at Make-Ready have faithfully translated two of Tomas’s hyperrealistic landscape paintings into print, capturing the depth of his Romantic-inspired palette and fidelity of his intricate brushstrokes.

subscriptionTag: Tomás Sánchez - El testigo by Tomás Sánchez
seoDescription: Collect a pair of limited edition prints by Tomás Sánchez that inspire a moment's meditation.
description:
In El testigo, Tomás Sánchez lets the transcendent power of golden hour live forever.

For nearly three decades, the Cuban artist has painted meditative landscapes in hyperrealistic detail. Here, his delicate brushstrokes render a canopy of foliage, while soft amber light creates a mesmerising atmosphere, drawing the viewer in. Towering treetops form arches "reminiscent of temples", beneath which two figures sit in quiet reflection – mirroring Tomás's own daily practice.

To create this edition, printers at Make-Ready translated the piece in exceptional detail, faithfully capturing the depth of Tomás's Romantic-inspired palette into print.

subscriptionTag: Shirin Neshat  - Unveiling series #1, 1993 & Unveiling series #2, 1993 by Shirin Neshat
seoDescription: Purchase a pair of limited edition prints by artist Shirin Neshat
description:
Collect a pair of hybrid silkscreen and photographic portraits by Shirin Neshat, based on her seminal body of work Women of Allah.

The work sees Farsi calligraphy handwritten by Shirin applied as a separate silkscreen layer to a powerful self portrait and image of the artist’s feet, both rendered in ultraviolet print by the printers at Make-Ready.
releaseNote: Unveiling series #1, 1993: Edition of 255 / Unveiling series #2, 1993: Edition of 161

subscriptionTag: Shirin Neshat  - Women Without Men #1, 2009 & Women Without Men #2, 2009 by Shirin Neshat
seoDescription: Collect a pair of limited edition prints by artist Shirin Neshat.
description:
Collect a pair of limited edition photographic prints by Shirin Nehsat, based on stills from her acclaimed film Women Without Men.

The Silver Lion-winning 2009 feature sees Shirin direct a story of Iranian women and their navigating of the social, political and environmental upheavals of their country following its CIA-backed coup d'état of left-leaning leader Mosaddegh in 1953. Like much of Shirin’s work, its lens focuses on where the personal and political collide.
releaseNote: Women Without Men #1, 2009: Edition of 118 / Women Without Men #2, 2009: Edition of 116

subscriptionTag: Oscar yi Hou - Coolieisms, aka: Born In The USA (Go And Kill The Yellow Man) by Oscar yi Hou
seoDescription: Collect a new limited edition print by Brooklyn-based portrait painter Oscar yi Hou.
description:
In this new limited edition print, Oscar yi Hou reimagines Bruce Springsteen's iconic Born in the U.S.A. album cover, infusing it with queer sensuality.

Our first collaboration with Oscar, Coolieisms, aka: Born In The USA (Go And Kill The Yellow Man), is a translation of the original oil painting from his ongoing Coolieisms series. The series title references a 19th-century slur historically used to degrade exploited Chinese railroad labourers. Through this body of work, Oscar explores East Asian queer experiences in America, blending American pop culture, queer masculinities, kink iconography, and references to both ancient and contemporary Asian art and culture.

In his take on the cover, Oscar replaces the all-American man with a figure dressed in leather fetish gear. Across the stripes of the flag, lyrics from Bruce Springsteen's original song – "go and kill the yellow man" – are layered, referencing US imperialism and its violent history in Asia.

The edition is rich with symbolic detail, from the figure's small gold hoop – mirroring the artist's piercing – to a glitter-embellished navy handkerchief, nodding to the queer practice of 'flagging' which originated in 1970s gay male and BDSM communities as a code to communicate your sexual preferences. To embellish these details, printers at Make-Ready applied a dynamic silkscreen high-gloss varnish to specific areas and used a dazzling glitter coating to highlight the stars of the US flag on the navy handkerchief.

subscriptionTag: Grayson Perry - Magical Thinking (Large) by Grayson Perry
seoDescription: Grayson Perry channels the whimsical charm of a Russian lubok print at vast scale in a limited edition print, now available to collect.
description:
In Magical Thinking (Large), Grayson Perry channels the whimsical charm of a Russian lubok print at vast scale.

The idea for Magical Thinking (Large) was sparked when Grayson encountered Cornelius de Vos’ Portrait of a Lady at the Wallace Collection in London. Here, he reimagines de Vos’ subject, encircling her with a constellation of words and symbols. The graphic composition draws inspiration from a 17th-century print style that pairs vivid illustration with narratives derived from literature, religious stories and folk tales.

To create the edition, printers at Make-Ready developed a bespoke textured paper that "fights back" against the ink. The result is a uniquely tactile silkscreen with intentional irregularities – a homage to the perfectly imperfect nature of woodblock prints.

subscriptionTag: Mickalene Thomas - November 1981 by Mickalene Thomas
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition glitter-embellished print by Mickalene Thomas which depicts an unapologetic portrait of sensuality.
description:
Desire takes centre stage in November, 1981.

In this sensual collage, Mickalene Thomas blends playfulness with social commentary on the performance of Black femme desire. The central image is cut out of Jet – an African American magazine founded in 1951. By appropriating an anonymous ‘beauty of the month’, Mickalene challenges notions of sex, power and erotica.

Through close collaboration between Mickalene’s studio and printmakers at Make-Ready, this edition captures the layered complexity of the original work. The anonymous woman is printed over a silver base layer, giving a lustrous sheen to her naked body and afro-crowned head. Glittery blue lines trace the contours of her form, while her lips are exaggerated with fluorescent pink. High-gloss varnish nods to the shiny finish of the original magazine.

subscriptionTag: Harland Miller - York So Good They Named It Once by Harland Miller
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by Harland Miller. York So Good They Named It Once sees the artist’s satirical takes on book covers get personal.
description:
Harland Miller gets personal with his novel painting in this new limited edition silkscreen print, in support of York Museums Trust.

Part of Harland's satirical spins on the publishing world, which he's become renowned for, York So Good They Named It Once sees the artist turn his attention to the region he calls home.

While a work in its own right, the printers at Make-Ready have translated the texture and detail of the original to a 27-colour print of incredible fidelity and quality. Harland's brushstrokes, and even a strand of hair suspended in paint, are captured in the edition.

subscriptionTag: Jonny Niesche - Musk romance in deepest blue by Jonny Niesche
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by Jonny Niesche which explores colour as a gateway to emotion and imagination.
description:
Jonny Niesche pushes the limits of blue in an emotive limited edition print.

Musk romance in deepest blue is based on the words of philosopher Gaston Bachelard, who saw colour as a gateway to emotion and imagination. The depth of feeling associated with navy is offset by sky blue, pointing towards lighter feelings such reverie and dreams. This rich interplay of colour is exemplar of Jonny's ability to bring a mirror-like quality to his work.

The edition is based upon an original textile work, refined into the medium of print. For the artist, the print will become complete once collectors have connected their own memories and emotions to the colours.

subscriptionTag: Tomás Sánchez - Cascada como ícono by Tomás Sánchez
seoDescription: Collect a pair of limited edition prints by Tomás Sánchez that inspire a moment's meditation.
description:
A cascading waterfall becomes a portal for reflection in a new limited edition print by Tomás Sánchez.

In many of his landscapes, Tomás introduces small meditating figures that represent the highest states of consciousness. Here, he depicts one such figure, captivated by nature's majesty. Through a canopy of treetops rendered in hyperrealistic detail, Tomás bathes the scene in the warm glow of golden hour – a time sacred to his meditation practice and symbolic of the cycles of "beginnings and endings to which we are all connected".

The edition meticulously translates the rich colours of one of Tomás's immersive oil paintings into print. Throughout the process, printmakers at Make-Ready focused on achieving exceptional fidelity and rich colouration – both critical objectives of Tomás’s work.

subscriptionTag: Jonny Niesche - Musk Romance in Deepest Blue and Champagne Lexus  by Jonny Niesche
seoDescription: Collect a diptych of limited edition prints by Jonny Niesche which explore colour as a gateway to emotion and imagination.
description:
Jonny Niesche’s two favourite works are paired in a tonal diptych.

Musk romance in deepest blue is based on the words of philosopher Gaston Bachelard, who saw colour as a gateway to emotion and imagination. The depth of feeling associated with navy is offset by sky blue, pointing towards lighter feelings such reverie and dreams.

Champagne Lexus sees blush pink dissolving into chocolate brown to form a playful shade of ‘Champagne’. For the artist, the specificity of this tone recalls a kitsch shade of automotive paint from his youth, as well as the techniques of artists such as Donald Judd.

subscriptionTag: Jammie Holmes - Fred by Jammie Holmes

subscriptionTag: Friedrich Kunath - Storms Never Last by Friedrich Kunath
seoDescription: Collect a hand-finished limited edition print by German artist Friedrich Kunath, Storms Never Last.
description:
Our latest collaboration with Friedrich Kunath, Storms Never Last, transforms the artist's original 2023 oil painting into a hand-finished print.

Drawing inspiration from Romanticism, Friedrich imbues his vivid, atmospheric works with poetic phrases, influenced by anything from 90s song lyrics and postcards to perfume scents. In this edition, a solitary figure seeks refuge from a storm. At the heart of the piece, a handwritten reflection, "Storms Never Last," offers comfort and consolation – "a silver lining to a rainy-day state of mind."

To create the edition, printmakers at Make-Ready faithfully translated the artist's intuitive brushstrokes from the original painting to print, capturing the tactile quality of the impasto oil paint while amplifying the clarity of its hidden messages. Each edition also bears unique bird drawings, hand-finished by the artist in acrylic paint.

subscriptionTag: Mickalene Thomas - Afro Goddess Looking Forward by Mickalene Thomas
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition glitter-embellished print by Mickalene Thomas which enshrines Black womanhood with a powerful self portrait.
description:
Mickalene Thomas is her own muse in a tableaux exploring self love.

As the Afro Goddess, Mickalene reclines on a couch haloed by her sparkling afro. The portrait centres on the unwavering gaze of the artist’s eyes – cut and pasted from a black and white self-portrait. The bold patterns on her clothes give way to a collaged backdrop that hints at a luxurious interior. Mickalene shrouds her image in the power that Black women are historically excluded from.

Afro Goddess Looking Forward is an early example of Mickalene’s now iconic visual language that blends printmaking, painting, and collage techniques. This faithful edition meticulously translates the original into an 8 layer silkscreen, embellished with glitters to emphasise the iridescence of her hair and clothes.

subscriptionTag: Judy Chicago - Let It All Hang Out by Judy Chicago
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by Judy Chicago. Heaven is for white men only marks a monumental shift in Judy's practice, telling her story of womanhood.
description:
Judy Chicago tells her story of womanhood in this limited edition print of her landmark 1973 painting.

Let It All Hang Out is a portrait of female pleasure and orgasm, symbolically represented by the central core and biomorphic shapes that ripple outwards – emblematic of Judy's unique yonic iconography that has come to define her career.

But back when Judy created this artwork, the idea of women enjoying sex was even more taboo than it remains today: "When I painted Let It All Hang Out, it scared me to death because it is about the power of female sexuality and the pulsing nature of female orgasm. I love that painting."

The print is embellished with a silkscreen shimmer layer, emulating the hypnotic irradiance of the original large-scale painting.

subscriptionTag: Mickalene Thomas - Landscape With Woman Washing Her Feet & Resist by Mickalene Thomas
seoDescription: Collect a pair of editions, each marking significant moments and themes within Mickalene's career.
description:
Mickalene Thomas recounts personal history and powerful notions of freedom in two rousing print editions.

Originally created in 2017, Resist spans nearly a century of African American history. Mickalene appropriates photojournalistic imagery that centres on moments of racist violence such as the Tulsa Race Massacre (1921), and police dogs attacking a civil rights protestor in Birmingham Alabama (1963). Alongside the brutality she interjects symbols of Black resistance, like protestors bearing ‘freedom’ placards and a portrait of writer and activist James Baldwin.

In Landscape With Woman Washing Her Feet, Mickalene brings her voice to Nicolas Poussin’s eponymous painting from 1650. The artist became enamoured by the romantic style of the Hudson River School painters after frequent travels to upstate New York in 2008. Using photographs taken during this time, she pieces together the idyllic scene – but the titular woman is absent. A flash of glittering animal print offers a clue at who she might have been.

subscriptionTag: Ferrari Sheppard - Iris by Ferrari Sheppard
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by Ferrari Sheppard.
description:
Our latest collaboration with Ferrari Sheppard, Iris, transforms his original 2022 oil painting of the same name into a shimmering limited edition silkscreen and digital print.

In Iris, Ferrari employs his signature gestural style to depict a solitary figure seated in a field of fluorescent blooms – "a place of her choosing, where she truly belongs". Inspired by the timeless enigma of the Mona Lisa, the artist wanted the portrait to be "contemplative, playful, and enigmatic", inviting the viewer to interpret her emotions for themselves.

To create the edition, printers at Make-Ready translated the luminosity of the figure's blouse (originally painted with 24K gold leaf) by using metallic inks and gold silkscreen layers, achieving a radiant, gilded effect in the print.

subscriptionTag: Sayre Gomez - America's Tire by Sayre Gomez
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by LA-based artist Sayre Gomez, bringing to life an 'America's Tire' billboard.
description:
In this new limited edition print by LA-based painter Sayre Gomez, glow-in-the-dark details enhance the artist's signature hyperrealism.

Sayre draws inspiration from the Los Angeles landscape, often depicting deserted strip malls and the bright glow of commercial signage in his photorealistic paintings. In this piece, that glow is intensified with phosphorescent ink, applied by the printers at Make-Ready – marking the artist’s first time working with the medium.

"I love the novelty that the phosphorescent adds," he says. "I always think that making an edition should have an additive quality. In this case, we were able to truly transform the original (America's Tire, 2022)."

subscriptionTag: Jordan Casteel, Derek Fordjour, Jenny Holzer, Hilary Pecis, Harland Miller, Adam Pendleton, Josh Smith - Amphorae
seoDescription: Collect a septet of ceramic amphorae designed by Jordan Casteel, Derek Fordjour, Jenny Holzer, Harland Miller, Hilary Pecis, Adam Pendleton and Josh Smith and launched in support of charity: water.
description:
Collect a septet of hand-painted ceramic amphorae, launched in support of charity: water.

Jordan Casteel, Derek Fordjour, Jenny Holzer, Harland Miller, Hilary Pecis, Adam Pendleton and Josh Smith each designed an amphora as part of a transatlantic collaboration between Artspace and Avant Arte, drawing on their wider practice as well as the vessel’s function and classical significance.

Proceeds will support charity: water in their endeavour to end the global water crisis.
releaseNote:
Editions of 30

Listed price reflects a saving of €1,000 per amphora. For smaller sets, email collecting@avantarte.com.

subscriptionTag: Shirin Neshat  - Women Without Men #1, 2009 by Shirin Neshat
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition photographic print, based on a still from Shirin Neshat's acclaimed film Women Without Men.
description:
Shirin Neshat turns an atmosphere-imbued visual from her acclaimed film Women Without Men into a limited edition photographic print.

In the 2009 film, her first feature, Shirin directs a story of Iranian women navigating the social, political, and environmental upheavals of their country following the CIA-backed coup d'état of the left-leaning Mosaddegh in 1953. Like much of Shirin’s work, its lens puts focus on where the personal and political collide.

Shirin, who has lived in exile for most of her adult life, is a vital advocate for women in Iran and beyond – shaping global conversations on identity and gender.

subscriptionTag: Ai Weiwei - Combat fear with truth by Ai Weiwei
seoDescription: Collect a signed, limited edition silkscreen print by Ai Weiwei. Created to celebrate the Year of the Snake, ‘Combat Fear With Truth’ pays tribute to an – in Weiwei’s eyes – unduly derided creature.
description:
Ai Weiwei pays tribute to a kindred serpentine spirit.

The second silkscreen in a series inspired by the Chinese Zodiac coincides with the Year of the Snake. Weiwei considers the snake an unduly derided creature – often feared and, like himself, liable to be misrepresented or misunderstood. In Weiwei’s depictions, such as monumental sculptures made from the school bags of earthquake victims or the life jackets of refugees, the snake becomes a conduit for truth.

Combat fear with truth is a precise 5-colour silkscreen created in close collaboration with printmakers at Make-Ready in London. Strategic overprinting, 10 layers in total, enhances the vivacity of each colour and adds depth to the surface of the artwork.

subscriptionTag: Taku Obata - B BOY JUSHI by Taku Obata
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition sculpture by Taku Obata. B BOY JUSHI transforms __ a hand-painted resin sculpture.
description:
B BOY JUSHI dances into resin in Taku Obata's dynamic collectable sculpture.

Captured in motion, the dancer’s fluid pose pays homage to Taku’s own experience in Japanese breakdancing crews. B BOY’s agility shines in a balancing act of angular limbs – his signature oversized hat and futuristic goggles lay perfectly vertical as he throws his body down to the floor. Clad in hand-painted neon pink streetwear, the character's energy is brought to life in vivid colour.

subscriptionTag: Adam Pendleton - Untitled (Blue Amphora) by Adam Pendleton
seoDescription: Collect a hand-painted ceramic amphora by Adam Pendleton, launched in support of charity: water. Untitled (Blue Amphora) belongs to a series of seven, conceived and crafted in a transatlantic collaboration between Artspace and Avant Arte.
description:
Collect a hand-painted ceramic amphora by Adam Pendleton, launched in support of charity: water.

In his earliest Black Dada paintings Adam Pendleton used only shades and tones of black, combining conceptual inspiration from serialised, logic-driven artworks like Incomplete Open Cubes (1974) by Sol LeWitt with layered, gestural applications of paint. More recently, he has introduced colour. In the case of the painting referenced by his amphora, ultramarine. The process of transformation – from two to three dimensions, from canvas to clay – echoes the sequential transformations and diverse media that characterise Adam’s practice.

The artwork belongs to a series of seven, conceived and crafted in a transatlantic collaboration between Artspace and Avant Arte. Proceeds will support charity: water in their endeavour to end the global water crisis.

subscriptionTag: George Condo - Fashion Model by George Condo
seoDescription: Collect a signed print by George Condo. In ‘Fashion Model’ the artist uses psychological cubism to expose the horror associated with the makings of a super star.
description:
George Condo balances the beautiful and the grotesque.

With long legs, sleek blonde hair and an archetypal pose, the subject of Fashion Model has the glamorous makings of a super star. Her picture-perfect image, however, is distorted by George’s ‘psychological cubism’ – an attempt to represent multiple mental states in a single portrait. To externalise the horror within, George portrays her head morphing into a nose lined with sets of teeth. In turn, the figure satirises the way pervasive beauty standards warp our perception of reality.

Fashion Model is the final instalment in a quartet of print editions launched in support of Dia Art Foundation. George’s painting has been meticulously translated into a 27 colour silkscreen in close collaboration with artisan printmakers at Make-Ready in London.
releaseNote: This draw includes an extra verification step. You will receive an email with more information upon entering the draw. This step needs to be completed before the draw closes, at 14:00 UK time on 18 February.

subscriptionTag: Barry McGee - Fuzz Gathering by Barry McGee
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by graffiti and fine art cult hero Barry McGee.
description:
Barry McGee hand-finishes a new limited edition print uniting signature motif and striking pattern.

The Bay Area’s favourite underground art son resurfaces his Everyman heads – an emblem of San Francisco’s marginalised communities and outsiders everywhere – resting them on bold geometric prints. Both come vividly to life in a silkscreen layer of neon ink rendered by the printers at Make-Ready.

Each edition bears a unique illustration, hand-drawn by the artist at the rear. The drawing is visible through a purpose-built window.

Also signed by the artist, this print represent the chance to own a one-off piece by Barry, a pioneer of the Mission School movement, that embodies his coexisting legend across fine art and graffiti.

subscriptionTag: Shirin Neshat  - Unveiling series #1, 1993 by Shirin Neshat
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by artist Shirin Neshat.
description:
Shirin Neshat employs her signature calligraphy and photography combination in a new limited edition print based on one of the artist’s most important works. It is finished with a separate silkscreen layer of Farsi, handwritten by Shirin.

This edition sits within the conceptual period of the artist’s seminal Women of Allah (1993-1997) series, a body of work that unpacks the interconnected nature of women’s bodies and political ideology.

subscriptionTag: Ai Weiwei - Circle in Black by Ai Weiwei
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition woodblock print by trailblazing artist Ai Weiwei. ‘Circle in black’ draws upon ancient printmaking methods and the raised middle finger from the artist’s seminal series, Study of perspective.
description:
Ai Weiwei uses an ancient art form to speak truth to power.

In Circle in Black, Weiwei arranges one of his most well known artistic symbols in a radial composition. The artist started using the motif of the middle finger in 1995 when taking photos for his seminal series Study of Perspective. In the series, Weiwei stuck up his middle finger to historic landmarks in an act of defiance that asserts our collective right to form, hold and express individual beliefs.

First used in ancient China, woodblock printing befits Weiwei’s interest in the artisanal processes that have been used to create significant objects through history. Each print is made by hand using a carved wooden block loaded with black ink, introducing unique variations in texture to the surface of the artwork.

subscriptionTag: James Jean - Maze - Lucid by James Jean
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition sculpture by Taiwanese-American artist James Jean based on his Maze character.
description:
James Jean captures the aura of Maze with a translucent sculpture.

For Maze (Lucid), James reimagines one of his enduring muses. First depicted in a 2008 painting, Maze is poised in a quiet moment of reflection. The character rests her hands upon a hoop enclosing a circular labyrinth,  representing the human quest to find freedom when following new paths. 

Her new-found translucency is achieved with a frosted resin casting. Refined over months to find the perfect levels of transparency and fidelity, the medium allows light to filter through the sculpture. The edition is accompanied with a detached labyrinth and stick, to be assembled upon arrival.

The artwork belongs to a series of seven, conceived and crafted in a transatlantic collaboration between Artspace and Avant Arte. Proceeds will support charity: water in their endeavour to end the global water crisis.

subscriptionTag: Shirin Neshat  - Women Without Men #2, 2009 by Shirin Neshat
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition photo print by Shirin Neshat, based on a still from her acclaimed film Women Without Men.
description:
Shirin Neshat turns a standout figurative shot from her acclaimed film Women Without Men into a special edition photographic print.

In the 2009 film, her first feature, Shirin directs a story of Iranian women navigating the social, political, and environmental upheavals of their country following the CIA-backed coup d'état of the left-leaning Mosaddegh in 1953. Like much of Shirin’s work, its lens puts focus on where the personal and political collide.

Shirin, who has lived in exile for most of her adult life, is a vital advocate for women in Iran and beyond – shaping global conversations on identity and gender.

subscriptionTag: Shirin Neshat  - Unveiling series #2, 1993 by Shirin Neshat
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by artist Shirin Neshat.
description:
Shirin Neshat employs her signature calligraphy and photography combination in a new limited edition print based on one of her most important works.

Farsi calligraphy handwritten by the artist is applied as a separate silkscreen layer to an image of her feet, rendered on UV pigment by the printers at Make-Ready.

This edition sits within the conceptual period of Shirin’s seminal Women of Allah (1993-1997) series, a body of work that unpacks the interconnected nature of women’s bodies and political ideology.

subscriptionTag: Jordan Casteel - Peak Summer by Jordan Casteel

Collect a hand-painted ceramic amphora by Jordan Casteel, launched in support of charity: water.

Jordan considers the paintings she makes of her garden self-portraits, in the sense that they encapsulate time spent cultivating, observing and documenting. Peak Summer takes one such painting as its starting point, encircling an amphora with a tangle of vines, leaves and flowers.

The artwork belongs to a series of seven, conceived and crafted in a transatlantic collaboration between Artspace and Avant Arte. Proceeds will support charity: water in their endeavour to end the global water crisis.

subscriptionTag: Anna Ridler - Price Per Stem by Price Per Stem
seoDescription: Discover an expansive body of work by Anna Ridler which explores the precarious price of peonies in relation to social, industrial, economic and environmental factors.
description:
Anna Ridler and the price of peonies.

Peonies are romantic and ephemeral. They are also a lucrative commodity. This paradox prompted Anna Ridler to excavate the social, industrial, economic and environmental factors hidden behind the flowers we take for granted in florists and supermarkets.

Price Per Stem is a series of 25 unique artworks. Each one comprises a paired physical and digital element.

The physical element entails 56 photographs of real peonies, taken by Anna in her studio. Once printed, each peony is annotated with its market price.

These photographs form the basis of the corresponding digital element – a single imagined peony in video form, generated from the 56 real peonies. To create her digital flowers, Anna created an intricate model based on data and events that influence the price of peonies, from fluctuations in weather to holidays like Valentine’s and Mother’s Day associated with surges in demand.

To complete the digital element, Anna traced choice moments from each peony and layered them over fluctuating prices. In this final step, the peonies are reconnected with the physical world.
releaseNote: Series of 25

subscriptionTag: Taku Obata - B BOY JUSHI by Taku Obata
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition sculpture by Taku Obata. B BOY JUSHI transforms __ a hand-painted resin sculpture.
description:
B BOY JUSHI dances into resin in Taku Obata's dynamic collectable sculpture.

Captured in motion, the dancer’s fluid pose pays homage to Taku’s own experience in Japanese breakdancing crews. B BOY’s agility shines in a balancing act of angular limbs – his signature oversized hat and futuristic goggles lay perfectly vertical as he throws his body down to the floor. Clad in hand-painted neon pink streetwear, the character's energy is brought to life in vivid colour.

subscriptionTag: Danielle Mckinney - Sandman by Danielle Mckinney
seoDescription: Sandman is a time limited print by Danielle Mckinney in which the image of the sleeping woman is emancipated from the white male gaze of art history.
description:
In Sandman, Danielle Mckinney explores the transformative power of dreams.

To Danielle, rest is sacred — particularly for the Black women who inhabit her paintings. Her edition’s title, Sandman, refers to a figure in European folklore that brings sleep and pleasant dreams by sprinkling magical sand in people’s eyes. Channeling this mythical figure, Danielle asks who deserves rest, and who is allowed to dream.

At the centre of the print is Danielle’s interpretation of Le Rêve, Picasso’s 1932 painting of his sleeping young mistress. The colour-blocked cubism stands out within Danielle’s earth-toned interior. Underneath the framed Picasso, another sleeping woman sinks into an olive green couch. Although she is fully nude, her depiction seems less voyeuristic than the exposed breast of Picasso’s subject. By including Le Rêve in Sandman, Danielle emancipates the image of the sleeping woman from the white male gaze of art history.

subscriptionTag: Jenny Holzer - Full by Jenny Holzer
seoDescription: Collect a hand-painted ceramic amphora by Jenny Holzer, launched in support of charity: water. Full belongs to a series of seven, conceived and crafted in a transatlantic collaboration between Artspace and Avant Arte.
description:
Collect a hand-painted ceramic amphora by Jenny Holzer, launched in support of charity: water.

Jenny Holzer’s texts make bold statements about the modern world. In their lyricism, however, the phrases expose the subjectivity and mutable character of truth. They instruct and inform, while questioning the ways individuals respond to their political, social, physical, psychological and personal environments. From her Survival texts, Jenny chose ‘IN A DREAM YOU SAW A WAY TO SURVIVE AND YOU WERE FULL OF JOY’ to encircle an amphora painted to resemble aged terracotta.

The artwork belongs to a series of seven, conceived and crafted in a transatlantic collaboration between Artspace and Avant Arte. Proceeds will support charity: water in their endeavour to end the global water crisis.

subscriptionTag: Will Cotton  - The Cowgirl from Will Cotton
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition glitter-embellished print by artist Will Cotton.
description:
The Cowgirl takes us on a ride across vanilla ice cream shores.

In Will Cotton’s candyland, desire and excess reign supreme. Our first print collaboration, The Cowgirl, is taken from a series of oil paintings that introduced a new cast of characters to the landscape. The titular cowgirl looks like a 50s pin-up star with her bedazzled costume, Old Hollywood waves, and million-dollar smile. She finds natural kinship with the elusive unicorn – both are "untamable, all-powerful creatures, desired by all."

Will’s impossible fantasies are rendered in realistic detail – like the muscle definition of the mythical creature in full gallop. His balance of traditional painting techniques and post-modern garishness is faithfully recreated using archival pigments. In line with the ‘more is more’ logic of Will’s land of desire, the print is finished with two silkscreen glitter layers on the cowgirl’s pistol and candy heart.

seoDescription: Collect a limited edition sculpture by Slawn. Ugly Bastard is a satirical self-portrait that is mischievous yet challenges conventions.
description:
Who are you calling ugly?

Slawn is best known for cartoonish artworks spray-painted on canvas and beyond. His distinctive scrawl expands into three dimensions as a limited edition sculpture. Ugly Bastard began as a satirical self portrait – equal parts irreverent and introspective. Now, he’s seeking a life of his own.

The figure is crouching – head bowed and gazed lowered like a sleek, modern gargoyle. He is painted in a hypnotic shade, carefully colour-matched to the underbelly of a Magic 8 ball. Look closely, and you’ll see your own reflection.

subscriptionTag: Kukwon Woo - Breakfast on the Beach by Woo Kuk Won
seoDescription: Collect a signed print by Kukwon Woo. ‘Breakfast on the beach’ places a fantastical twist on a biblical breakfast scene.
description:
Kukwon Woo presents a biblical story as an East Asian idyll.

‘Breakfast on the Beach’ is a ukiyo-e inspired landscape, trading the motif of the snow-capped mountain for a village on a hill by the sea. The picturesque scene is framed by text on two sides in two scripts. The vertical hanzi text replicates the traditional signatures on a woodblock print, where a bible reference lies.

John 21 opens with the ‘Breakfast on the beach’ that gives this edition its title. In the biblical story, the resurrected Jesus miraculously fills the nets of his tired disciples, and cooks them fish by the Sea of Galilee. In Woo’s rendition, Jesus sits under a striped parasol. He is joined at the table by the strawberry-blonde toddler and white dog that recur in Woo’s paintings. Across the top, a verse from the passage beckons you to the feast in Woo’s looping roman script.

This endearing image of togetherness is printed in 13 layers, faithfully recreating the texture of Woo’s painting.

subscriptionTag: Miwa Komatsu - White and Black Guiding Yamainu-sama by Miwa Komatsu
seoDescription: Collect a two-part, limited edition sculpture by Japanese artist Miwa Komatsu, inspired by the divine beings who have guided her since childhood and finished by hand in her studio.
description:
Miwa Komatsu enshrines her lifelong spirit guides with a pair of hand-painted sculptures.

Yamainu are divine beings, found in various forms throughout Japanese folklore. Miwa has cherished their guidance throughout her life. The creatures appear – wide eyed and cosmic – in many of her paintings.

An edition in two parts – one white, one black – explores harmony and contrast. Details on the surface of each sculpture are painted by the artist in her studio, making every pair unique. They include vines, wolf hair, cherubim wings and the traditional Japanese kanoko motif.

subscriptionTag: Cristina de Miguel - Tentacular Thinking by Cristina de Miguel
seoDescription: Collect limited edition print by Cristina de Miguel. In Tentacular Thinking, expressive strokes dance together.
description:
Untamed bodies tangle in a hand-finished silkscreen by Cristina de Miguel.

In Tentacular Thinking, two figures partake in a frenetic dance. The title refers to an egalitarian worldview where humans, animals, plants, and even machines, are seen as parts of an interconnected whole. Cristina’s semi-abstract subjects and wild compositions help us see beyond the confines of our bodies and everyday lives.

Cristina worked closely with printmakers to transform her artwork into an edition of silkscreen prints before hand-finishing them with oil sticks in her studio, making each one unique.

subscriptionTag: Alpha Centauri Kid - Wonderland by Alpha Centauri Kid
seoDescription: Collect an original artwork by Alpha Centauri Kid. ‘Wonderland’ is a textured UV pigment print with spot varnish details, and belongs to a new body of work inspired by Vincent Van Gogh, Shakespeare and paradise.
description:
The Cheshire Cat grins into focus as piano keys spiral down the rabbit hole in a print by Alpha Centauri Kid.

Wonderland is one of two works from Piano Blossoms inspired by Lewis Carroll’s Alice. In both cases, a.c.k. considers what other mysteries hide behind the looking glass.

Unlike earlier works which introduce glitches to obscure figures, the artwork began as an abstract landscape. a.c.k. then scoured the composition for hidden figures he could unearth by tweaking colours, defining outlines and reordering layers.

The 12k digital artwork was transformed into a physical object by printmakers at Make-Ready in London, who worked closely with a.c.k. to introduce layers of texture and glossy highlights to the surface of the print.

subscriptionTag: Alpha Centauri Kid - Tempted in the Garden by Alpha Centauri Kid
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by Alpha Centauri Kid. ‘tempted in the Garden’ is a textured UV pigment print, and belongs to a new body of work inspired by Vincent van Gogh, Shakespeare and paradise.
description:
Star-crossed lovers take shelter in a tale of love and fate by Alpha Centauri Kid.

For our second collaboration a.c.k. set out to create a body of work inspired by Romeo and Juliet. In the end, the Muse led him in a different direction. Piano Blossoms emerged – a dreamy ode to music and the Muse with all the romance of a Shakespearean play.

Eventually, the tragic couple found refuge amongst the foliage of Eden. The more defined of the pair is Juliet, who is not only analogous to Biblical Eve, but also to the artist’s Muse. Hovering above her head is the apple that spelled humanity’s banishment from the garden. On her right is a memento mori in the form of a ghostly skull. These omens of tragedy are easily missed amongst the alluring gold flowers that illuminate the print.

The 12k digital artwork was transformed into a physical object by printmakers at Make-Ready in London, who worked closely with a.c.k. to introduce layers of texture to the surface of the print.

seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by trailblazing digital artist Beeple based on the signal state of his first generative artwork, The Tree of Knowledge – signed and numbered, with free worldwide shipping.
description:
Reality is subjective. Choose signal.

The Tree of Knowledge is a digitally-programmed sculpture which responds in real time to events around the world, with three possible states – signal, noise and violence. The artwork, part of the Lingotto collection, encompasses Beeple’s reflections on the subjective nature of our individual realities, and on a hypothetical symbiosis between technology and nature.

SIGNAL is the most optimistic state. A step back from the noise and violence of reality, it presents a measured, forward-thinking view in which humans, nature and technology manage to coexist.

Printmakers at Make-Ready in London have transformed a static representation of the tree in its signal state into a fine-tuned UV pigment print with a satin varnish seal.

seoDescription: Framing Options | Monica, 2024

subscriptionTag: Johnson Tsang - The Moment by Johnson Tsang
