Two become one in a surreal edition by Johnson Tsang.

The Moment is based on a porcelain sculpture, masterfully carved by Johnson in his workshop. A couple kiss within a hollow face – the owner of the face seemingly preoccupied by romance. For Johnson, the artwork represents the optimistic possibilities when we open our minds to love.

subscriptionTag: Ai Weiwei - Everyone is a dragon by Ai Weiwei
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition silkscreen print by trailblazing artist Ai Weiwei, created to mark the year of the dragon. ‘Everyone is a Dragon’ draws inspiration from the artist’s works in lego and a seminal exhibition on Alcatraz.
description:
Lego blocks become silkscreen squares in a dazzling print by Ai Weiwei.

The dragon is a familiar subject for Ai Weiwei – an allegory for the power of the individual, and the importance of freedom. Conceived to mark the year of the dragon in the Chinese zodiac, Everyone is a dragon transforms the pixel-like compositions of his iconic works in Lego into an elaborate silkscreen print. Fittingly, printmakers at Make-Ready in London used the same ink supplier as Lego to create it. Precise alignment and strategic overprinting deliver sharp edges and intense saturation.

subscriptionTag: Yoon Hyup - City Fountain by Yoon Hyup
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by Youn Hyup. City Fountain distils the bustling energy of Manhattan into a calming reflection of lights on water.
description:
In a new print, Yoon Hyup finds respite amidst the chaos of Manhattan. 

City Fountain is based on the artist’s imagined memory of wandering through New York, as vibrantly lit street vendors emerge beneath the darkening sky. Hyup pauses at a water fountain, captivated by the reflections of dazzling electric lights. The energy of the shimmering lights and echoing sound of the city are captured in his elegant line and dot, as the frenzy of New York continues far after the sun sets.

subscriptionTag: Derek Fordjour - Horn Trot Round by Derek Fordjour

Collect a hand-painted ceramic amphora by Derek Fordjour, launched in support of charity: water.

Translated to the cylindrical form of an amphora, the parade never ends.

The artwork belongs to a series of seven, conceived and crafted in a transatlantic collaboration between Artspace and Avant Arte. Proceeds will support charity: water in their endeavour to end the global water crisis.

subscriptionTag: Alpha Centauri Kid - Muse blossoms by Alpha Centauri Kid
seoDescription: Collect an original artwork by Alpha Centauri Kid. ‘Muse blossoms’ is a textured UV pigment print with spot varnish details, and belongs to a new body of work inspired by Vincent Van Gogh, Shakespeare and paradise.
description:
In Muse blossoms, Alpha Centauri Kid locates his elusive source of inspiration.

When beginning his latest body of work, a.c.k. did not feel the guidance of The Muse. He listened for Her whispers in music, and sought Her approval through artistic trial and error. When he found the right path, he realised it had taken him full circle – the work would be about inspiration itself, personified by his Muse.

Muse blossoms depicts The Muse as She once appeared to a.c.k. “This is Her, playing my Steinway.” We see only a slither of Her red gown, and Her guiding hand, resting on the keys. Over the scene, a.c.k. superimposes his reinterpretation of Almond Blossoms (1890) – borrowing Van Gogh’s seminal series as a symbol for artistic devotion.

The 12k digital artwork was transformed into a physical object by printmakers at Make-Ready in London, who worked closely with a.c.k. to introduce layers of texture and glossy highlights to the surface of the print.

seoDescription: Collect a limited edition artwork by Vhils. ‘Dissipate’ applies the street artist’s principle of creative destruction to print.
description:
A portrait stares through an acid haze in Dissipate by Alexandre Farto, aka Vhils.

The striking face of an anonymous woman is set against the backdrop of a city, the identity of which is also a mystery. Vhils applies his principle of creative destruction to the artwork, finding beauty in the unpredictable effects of acid. The result is an array of electric colours spread throughout a black veil rendered in delicate half-tone dots. 

The final corroded image has been captured as a limited edition giclée print.

subscriptionTag: Harland Miller - R U OK? by Harland Miller
seoDescription: Collect a hand-painted ceramic amphora by Harland Miller, launched in support of charity: water. R U OK? belongs to a series of seven, conceived and crafted in a transatlantic collaboration between Artspace and Avant Arte.
description:
Collect a hand-painted ceramic amphora by Harland Miller, launched in support of charity: water.

Based on a painting of the same name, R U OK? poses a question, also a greeting, in its simplest form. Harland’s use of abbreviation calls to mind rapid online communication, and contrasts it with the time taken to impart the phrase on canvas. Within the abstract composition, letters become objects – warped by the curvature of the amphora they surround.

The artwork belongs to a series of seven, conceived and crafted in a transatlantic collaboration between Artspace and Avant Arte. Proceeds will support charity: water in their endeavour to end the global water crisis.

subscriptionTag: Taku Obata - B Boy Seidou by Taku Obata
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition sculpture by Taku Obata. B BOY SEIDOU transforms a chiselled wooden b-boy into matte black painted bronze.
description:
A b-boy holds his form forever in a bronze sculpture by Taku Obata.

With his dynamic sculptures, Taku Obata demonstrates an understanding of the human body as a finely-balanced instrument. B BOY SEIDOU transforms the interlocking planes of one of his chiselled wooden dancers into painted bronze (seidou) – monochromatic, to emphasise the rakish angles and parallel planes within his pose. The b-boy’s oversized hat, balanced precariously on his head, and futuristic visor, extending far beyond his face, are both recurring motifs in Taku’s sketches and sculptures.

subscriptionTag: Kukwon Woo - Valley of the shadow of death & Breakfast on the beach [Diptych] by Kukwon Woo
seoDescription: Collect a signed print by Kukwon Woo. In ‘Valley of the Shadow of Death ’ and cultural influences collide while ‘Breakfast on the beach’ places a fantastical twist on a biblical breakfast scene.
description:
Kukwon Woo places a fantastical twist on two biblical scenes.

‘Valley of the Shadow of Death’ combines two popular metaphors for the battle between good and evil. The first is from Psalm 23, a biblical prayer for comfort and strength in the face of evil. The second is from the Star Wars: Empire Strikes Back, the science-fiction blockbuster.

‘Breakfast on the Beach’ is Woo’s rendition of the biblical passage John 21. In his version, Jesus sits under a striped parasol. He is joined at the table by the strawberry-blonde toddler and white dog that recur in Woo’s paintings. Across the top, a verse from the passage beckons you to the feast in Woo’s looping roman script.

subscriptionTag: Hank Willis Thomas - 'The only bond worth anything between human beings is their humanness' by Hank Willis Thomas
seoDescription: Hank Willis Thomas explores the social and historical meaning of sport through a print edition portraying the figure of Jesse Owens.
description:
Experience the intensity of the 1936 Olympics in a new print from conceptual artist Hank Willis Thomas.

"The only bond worth anything between human beings is their humanness." explores the social and historical meaning of sport through the figure of Jesse Owens. The record breaking athlete launches at full power across the paper, racing in the 100 metre dash. He wears collaged clothing in red and doily patterned white. A blue background, also collaged, introduces the third colour of the American flag.

The print is based on a new original work by Hank Willis Thomas currently on view in Paris, the host city for the 2024 Olympics. To replicate the dynamic texture of the original, printmakers built up variable height in nine layers of UV cured ink

subscriptionTag: Parra - FOUR WALLS by Piet Parra

description: A group of Neo-pop figures gather in two silkscreen editions by Parra. FOUR WALLS captures the hazy aftermath of a party in a contemplative and timeless scene. Meanwhile, chaos arises amongst the beach setting of LOST KEYS.

subscriptionTag: Alpha Centauri Kid - interblossom byAlpha Centauri Kid
seoDescription: Collect an original artwork by Alpha Centauri Kid. ‘interblossom’ is a textured UV pigment print with spot varnish details, and belongs to a new body of work inspired by Vincent Van Gogh, Shakespeare and paradise.
description:
Alpha Centauri Kid returns to an unpublished work from years gone by.

In interblossom, a.c.k. reimagines a scene from sci-fi movie Interstellar in which robot TARS – rendered here as an arrangement of interlocking keyboards – travels to Miller, a planet completely covered by water.

The work came back to life when refracted through the prism of Piano Blossoms. An unusual combination of purple and yellow dominates the composition. a.c.k. introduced flashes of green and pink to balance the palette. The resulting landscape is uncanny – like the world viewed through a mirror.

The 12k digital artwork was transformed into a physical object by printmakers at Make-Ready in London, who worked closely with a.c.k. to introduce layers of texture and glossy highlights to the surface of the print.

subscriptionTag: Dominique Fung - Handheld Fan by Dominique Fung
seoDescription: Collect limited edition print by Dominique Fung. Handheld Fan is a surreal honey-hued print that challenges Orientalist tropes.
description:
Dominique Fung reconfigures colonial-era visual tropes in this new limited edition print.

Handheld Fan exemplifies the artist’s distinctive blend of the uncanny and the symbolically charged. Based on her 2021 oil painting Bone Holding Fan, the work features four faces merging into a veiled Qing Dynasty bone hand fan. These fans, often intricately carved from bone or ivory and embellished with miniature paintings, calligraphy, or pierced latticework, were once luxury objects tied to courtly life and export markets.

Here, the fan emerges as a recurring motif, historically used in 18th and 19th-century European chinoiserie painting and early Hollywood cinema to exoticise and obscure Asian women. Whether delicately shielding a gaze or acting as an ornamental cypher, the fan operates as a stand-in for a racialised and gendered fantasy that Fung critically dismantles and reimagines through fragmentation and multiplicity.

Working in close collaboration with Fung, master printmakers at Make-Ready employed 13 layers of textured ink to create a raised outline around the fan, enhancing the tactile depth of the composition and echoing the artist’s engagement with material history and cultural memory.

subscriptionTag: Hilary Pecis - Lily Pond by Hilary Pecis

Collect a hand-painted ceramic amphora by Hilary Pecis, launched in support of charity: water.

Hilary Pecis paints the kinds of moments that easily pass us by. In doing so, she enshrines their beauty and importance. Her study of lilies and lily pads on the surface of a pond emerged as the perfect reference for her amphora – adapted such that its aquatic composition has no beginning or end.

The artwork belongs to a series of seven, conceived and crafted in a transatlantic collaboration between Artspace and Avant Arte. Proceeds will support charity: water in their endeavour to end the global water crisis.

subscriptionTag: Claire Tabouret - Paysage d’Intérieur (printemps) by Claire Tabouret
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition tapestry by Claire Tabouret. Paysage d’Intérieur (printemps) depicts an enchanted garden erupting in thousands of stitches.
description:
A spring garden by Claire Tabouret erupts in over 410,000 stitches.

In Paysage d’Intérieur an enchanting scene is translated into delicate embroidery. The edition focuses on light and materiality, an evolution of Claire’s ‘fluff’ paintings – a series of abstract works in which bold brushstrokes toy with the verdant landscapes of post-impressionist painters. With 20 colours, from lemon yellow to sea green and electric blue, Claire assembles a new vision for her original textured painting.

From thread and fabric to framing, every element of the artwork is crafted and assembled in Lyon – the birthplace of artisanal French textiles.

seoDescription: Collect an original artwork by Alpha Centauri Kid. ‘Golden Afternoon’ is a textured UV pigment print with spot varnish details, and belongs to a new body of work inspired by Vincent Van Gogh, Shakespeare and paradise.

In Golden Afternoon, a pink-shifted piano sprawls across a field of green.

The keys start to fade and suddenly vanish into the scene – like transitioning from a lullaby into a dream. The work is titled after the preface poem to Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland by Lewis Carroll that describes a joyful and idyllic childhood. In Disney's adaptation, the poem is set to music and sung by a chorus of flowers. In his, Alpha Centauri Kid presents child-like wonder through the filter of nostalgia.

description:
A face cuts through traffic in an acid print by Alexandre Farto, aka Vhils.

Blur sees street artist Vhils bring his abrasive methodology to silkscreen printing. The artwork is composed of two overlapping images – a busy street and a striking portrait. Both are intentionally anonymous. The artist presents an arresting metaphor for life in the big city, where cultural uniqueness is often overridden by the intensity of urban life.

Prints from the edition are individually hand-finished using quick ink and acid – eroding the surface of the artwork. In doing so, Vhils resists uniformity and blurs the lines between creation and destruction.

subscriptionTag: Jack Kaido  - ICYMI, 2024 by Jack Kaido
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print and accompanying NFT by Jack Kaido. ICYM is an amalgamation of digital perspectives.
description:
Jack Kaido gathers digital memories in print.

ICYMI is an amalgamation of the places and perspectives that have been core to Kaido’s practice and personal life. Fractured layers of colour are interwoven with components of the internet and software. The title, an abbreviation for ‘in case you missed it,’ acts as a reminder of the digital age’s influence on language.

seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by trailblazing digital artist Beeple based on the violence state of his first generative artwork, The Tree of Knowledge – signed and numbered, with free worldwide shipping.
description:
Reality is subjective. Choose violence.

The Tree of Knowledge is a digitally-programmed sculpture which responds in real time to events around the world, with three possible states – signal, noise and violence. The artwork, part of the Lingotto collection, encompasses Beeple’s reflections on the subjective nature of our individual realities, and on a hypothetical symbiosis between technology and nature.

VIOLENCE is a state of conflict. Activated at the push of a button, Beeple has placed an upper limit on the number of times it can be triggered before the tree remains aflame forever. With this mechanic he makes the point that, outside of the simulation, there is also an upper limit on the number of times we can make this choice before our reality is damaged beyond repair.

Printmakers at Make-Ready in London have transformed a static representation of the tree during its choose violence sequence into a fine-tuned UV pigment print with a satin varnish seal.

subscriptionTag: Parra - FOUR WALLS by Piet Parra
seoDescription: Collect a silkscreen print by Piet Parra. FOUR WALLS is a timeless depiction of a late night conversation between three guests in the final moments of a party.
description:
A trio of women luxuriate in a silkscreen print by Parra.

FOUR WALLS captures the hazy aftermath of a party in a contemplative and timeless scene. The guests sprawl over the floor, engaged in conversation that wanders between everything and nothing. Parra captures the feeling of being caught in a late-night moment, where time and place becomes blurred.

A strong dialogue between printmaker and artist allowed an original twist on the reference work to develop. The figures have a delicate gloss achieved by layering solid, seamless colour – overlapping in places to echo Parra’s painting techniques.

description:
TIDE perches his wooden cat on a precipice. 

In his paintings, TIDE sets cartoon cats within realistic scenes. With Sit, he echoes this juxtaposition in three dimensions. Polished walnut wood brings the smooth contours of his sculpture to life – a cartoon companion for the material world.

subscriptionTag: Iskra Velitchkova - Eyenessless by Iskra Velitchkova
seoDescription: Collect a unique generative print by Iskra Velitchkova. In EYELESSNESS, ocular, lens-like forms echo the artist’s reading of generative art as a tool for self reflection.
description:
Iskra Velitchkova plays reverse engineer to mother nature in a series of generative prints.

Iskra has a unique take on the relationship between humans and machines. She asks whether, by amplifying the immaterial parts of ourselves, machines can make us more human than ever.

This question runs in parallel to the seemingly-organic forms found throughout her practice. The apparition of such forms in generative outputs underscores our inevitable presence in the machines we make. When they do emerge, Iskra “refines, provokes and re-invents” them to better understand the resemblance – echoing nature’s happy accidents within her own coded creations in a process she likens to reverse engineering.

EYENESSLESS builds upon another series, Lines and Bones. Ocular, lens-like forms embody the themes of distance and perception that persist in Iskra’s theoretical framework. The artworks look back, echoing her reading of generative art as a tool for introspection, or a second self.

Close collaboration with printmakers at Make-Ready in London, using cutting edge printing technology, introduced another layer of interface between human and technology to the project – informing the code itself and placing unexpected emphases within its outputs.
releaseNote: Each unique print is paired with a matching NFT. Artworks will be allocated at random and revealed upon claiming.

seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by trailblazing digital artist Beeple based on the noise state of his first generative artwork, The Tree of Knowledge – signed and numbered, with free worldwide shipping.
description:
Reality is subjective. Choose noise.

The Tree of Knowledge is a digitally-programmed sculpture which responds in real time to events around the world, with three possible states – signal, noise and violence. The artwork, part of the Lingotto collection, encompasses Beeple’s reflections on the subjective nature of our individual realities, and on a hypothetical symbiosis between technology and nature.

NOISE is a state of saturation. Inspired by the overwhelming volume of conflicting information provided by modern media, it captures the feeling of hopelessness spawned by an endless stream of hot takes, crises and quandries.

Printmakers at Make-Ready in London have transformed an array of noise state trees into a fine-tuned UV pigment print with a satin varnish seal.

subscriptionTag: Danielle Mckinney - Shelter by Danielle Mckinney
seoDescription: Shelter is a limited edition print by Danielle McKinney pondering the natural rhythms of metamorphosis.
description:
A serene portrait by Danielle Mckinney ponders the rhythms of metamorphosis.

Shelter depicts a woman alone with her daydreams. Cocooned in her coat, she is visited by a Monarch butterfly which rests at the tip of her finger beyond her gaze. Butterflies often appear in Mckinney’s work to signal transformation and cyclical rhythms, while the subject’s red fingernails – another signature – symbolise smaller, everyday changes. Shelter invites us to reflect on our own moments of transformation and the quiet beauty found in contemplative solitude.

The edition meticulously translates the rich colours of one of Mckinney’s first oil paintings into print.  Each is finished with deckled edges and flashes of gold leaf, applied by hand to the wings of the butterfly.

subscriptionTag: Ai Weiwei - To Be Looked At... by Ai Weiwei
seoDescription: Ai Weiwei turns the camera on his collectors with an edition of sculptures in cut aluminium.
description:
Ai Weiwei turns the camera on collectors with an edition of sculptures in cut aluminium.

Surveillance and Weiwei have history. Drawing together personal experiences and societal shifts, he notes that security is often used as a guise for control and that, because of this, surveillance represents power.

To Be Looked At… takes the form of a bank of CCTV cameras, pointing in multiple directions for uninterrupted vision. The sculpture can be mounted on a wall or displayed on a horizontal surface.

Installed in homes around the world, the cameras and their pseudo-surveillance capture Weiwei’s wry humour. At the same time, they encapsulate an experience that has become an inescapable part of being alive.

subscriptionTag: Alpha Centauri Kid - Tempted in the Garden by Alpha Centauri Kid
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by Alpha Centauri Kid. ‘tempted in the Garden’ is a textured UV pigment print, and belongs to a new body of work inspired by Vincent van Gogh, Shakespeare and paradise.
description:
Star-crossed lovers take shelter in a tale of love and fate by Alpha Centauri Kid.

For our second collaboration a.c.k. set out to create a body of work inspired by Romeo and Juliet. In the end, the Muse led him in a different direction. Piano Blossoms emerged – a dreamy ode to music and the Muse with all the romance of a Shakespearean play.

Eventually, the tragic couple found refuge amongst the foliage of Eden. The more defined of the pair is Juliet, who is not only analogous to Biblical Eve, but also to the artist’s Muse. Hovering above her head is the apple that spelled humanity’s banishment from the garden. On her right is a memento mori in the form of a ghostly skull. These omens of tragedy are easily missed amongst the alluring gold flowers that illuminate the print.

The 12k digital artwork was transformed into a physical object by printmakers at Make-Ready in London, who worked closely with a.c.k. to introduce layers of texture to the surface of the print.

subscriptionTag: Ai Weiwei - Circle in Blue by Ai Weiwei
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition silkscreen print by trailblazing artist Ai Weiwei. ‘Circle in Blue’ riffs on the raised middle finger from the artist’s seminal series, Study of Perspective.
description:
Ai Weiwei raises his middle finger once again in a silkscreen tondo.

In Circle in Blue, Weiwei’s iconic gesture radiates outwards in a continuous composition. Weiwei started using the motif of the middle finger in 1995 when taking photos for his series Study of Perspective. In the series, Weiwei stuck up his middle finger to historic landmarks in an act of defiance that asserts our collective right to form, hold and express individual beliefs. For the artist, the power of a simple gesture like this is that anyone can make it.

The artwork is printed in 11 layers at Make-Ready in London. Its blue and white palette, lustrous finish and circular form call to mind Weiwei’s porcelain sculptures which themselves reference ancient Chinese ceramics from the Yuan and Ming dynasties.

subscriptionTag: Grayson Perry - Magical Thinking by Grayson Perry
seoDescription: Collect a silkscreen print by Grayson Perry. ‘Magical Thinking’ exposes the layer of mystical subjectivity through which we each engage with reality – signed and numbered, with free worldwide shipping.
description:
Grayson Perry thinks magically for a silkscreen print launched in support of the Contemporary Art Society.

Magical Thinking began when Grayson encountered a painting by Cornelis de Vos at the Wallace Collection in London. In a graphic composition inspired by traditional Russian lubki, he surrounds his own version of de Vos’ unidentified subject with a constellation of words and symbols. The work’s title references the layer of mystical subjectivity through which we each engage with reality.

Grayson worked closely with printmakers at Make-Ready in London to bring his vision to life. The result is a tactile silkscreen on bespoke textured paper with intentional irregularities – an homage to traditions from centuries ago, and a celebration of modern silkscreen printing.

subscriptionTag: Alpha Centauri Kid - Flower Demons by Alpha Centauri Kid
seoDescription: Collect an original artwork by Alpha Centauri Kid. ‘Flower Demons’ is a textured UV pigment print with spot varnish details, and belongs to a new body of work inspired by Vincent Van Gogh, Shakespeare and paradise.
description:
In Flower Demons, the underworld is nothing to be afraid of.

Branches grow from the head of a warmly lit figure – blossoming and winding as they reach into the darkness at the outer edges of the print. In the foreground, the figure’s hands play a crooked piano. Alpha Centauri Kid calls this supernatural musician a flower demon.

When beginning his latest body of work, ACK did not feel the guidance of the Muse – an energy that assures him he’s aligned with his purpose. Eventually, he stumbled upon Piano Blossoms as an overarching theme, and knew he was on the right path. Every artwork in the series became a reflection of his pursuit of the Muse. On this occasion, the same path also led him to an encounter with another supernatural being.

The 12k digital artwork was transformed into a physical object by printmakers at Make-Ready in London, who worked closely with a.c.k. to introduce layers of texture and glossy highlights to the surface of the print.

subscriptionTag: Parra - LOST KEYS by Piet Parra
seoDescription: Collect a silkscreen print by Piet Parra. LOST KEYS references the artist’s nostalgic memories of Amsterdam from years gone by.
description:
Parra depicts quiet chaos by the sea.

LOST KEYS is a nostalgic snapshot, paying homage to the playful beach scenes painted by Parra’s father in the 90s. Surrounded by sand dunes, three expressive women gesture as one appears to drop something. When creating the composition, Parra drew upon his personal life in Amsterdam, from the nearby sandy hills that he often cycles through to the title of a song by his band.

Parra’s sophisticated use of colour includes many colours that sit next to each other on the colour wheel. This provided a challenge to the printmakers, requiring many rounds to perfect the colour inks for the silkscreen print. Printed in a painterly fashion, light colours are layered over dark colours to foreground the figures.

subscriptionTag: José Parlá - The American Mindscape, Textured by José Parlá
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by José Parlá, launched to coincide with a homecoming exhibition in Miami and inspired by his expansive view of America and the Cuban diaspora.
description:
A print by José Parlá thrums with his expansive vision of America.

The American Mindscape will appear in an upcoming exhibition at the Pérez Art Museum in Miami. To mark José's return to the city where he was born, we’ve transformed the cacophonous painting into a limited edition print.

The painting itself began in 2021, when José was recovering from a four month coma and protests were erupting in Cuba. Layer upon layer of abstract marks and script embody entangled feelings of hope and anger, and represent the millions who since 1959 have joined Cuba’s diaspora. Extrapolating, José also reflects on the entire American continent, and the countless stories that connect its inhabitants in pursuit of freedom – asking what it really means to be American.

subscriptionTag: Antony Micallef - Portrait of Francis Bacon by Antony Micallef
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print by Antony Micallef. Portrait of Francis Bacon probes the limits of printmaking, using 57 layers of UV-cured ink to replicate the energetic impasto of the artist’s work in oil paint.
description:
A visceral tribute by Antony Micallef probes the limits of printmaking.

In his painting inspired by Lucian Freud’s portrait of Francis Bacon, Antony Micallef favoured thick, abstract impasto over discernable human features. Micallef shares an affinity with both artists and their raw representation of human forms. With Portrait of Francis Bacon, Micallef echoes the way Bacon used paint to elicit an emotional response, not only to the painted image, but to the physical condition of the paint itself.

Printmakers at Make-Ready worked closely with Micallef to achieve something he initially thought impossible. Layer upon layer of cured ink and satin varnish recreate the depth and texture of his painting, including a section where solidified paint extends beyond the edge of the canvas.

The edition was conceived in collaboration with Bridgeman Images and the Lucian Freud Archive.

subscriptionTag: Kukwon Woo - Valley of the Shadow of Death by Woo Kuk Won
seoDescription: Collect a signed print by Kukwon Woo. ‘Breakfast on the beach’
description:
Kukwon Woo reaches across time, genre and philosophy in a satirical culture clash.

‘Valley of the Shadow of Death’ combines two popular metaphors for the battle between good and evil. The first is from Psalm 23, a biblical prayer for comfort and strength in the face of evil. The second is from the Star Wars: Empire Strikes Back, the science-fiction blockbuster. Woo reimagines Luke Skywalker and Darth Vader’s infamous duel on Cloud City on earthly terrain. 

The duellers appear miniscule on a high mountain bridge, each wielding lightsabers like crosses at the head of a procession. Viewed in perspective, their grand battle appears inconsequential – like a game of dress up. However, Woo’s scrawled prayer reintroduces existential fears passed down through millenia.

Our textured print edition is based on an original painting by Woo, which in turn was inspired by Japanese Ukiyo-e prints.

seoDescription: Pejac creates an edition of 1000 unique prints, based on a hospital mural painted in his hometown during the pandemic.
description:
HOPE is a series of 1000 unique prints which revisits a mural painted on the wall of a Spanish hospital in 2020.

Pejac created the mural to remember the tragedies of Covid-19, but also the togetherness the pandemic fostered in communities around the world. Thousands of tiny figures form the illusion of a crevice. On close inspection, each has their own story, interacting with empathy and solidarity.

During a month-long residency at Make-Ready in London, Pejac reinterpreted his crevice on a blank canvas. The process was documented 1000 times. Each stage corresponds with a unique print. As a final flourish, one figure from each print is highlighted by hand with 24 carat gold leaf. In this figure, the artist hopes the viewer can see themselves shining amongst the crowd.

The images on this page show print 15/1000, selected as a representative example for prints 1-125. A minimum of 20 prints from this drop will be available at launch.

Lea and Monica are a pair of limited edition prints belonging to Gabriel Moses' series Regina – a photographic tribute to the women who have shaped his world.

The images epitomise Moses' ability to build timeless images that revisit the same world again and again, yet capture the individual spirit of his subjects.

subscriptionTag: Magdalena Suarez Frimkess - Homage for Jasper Johns by Magdalena Suarez Frimkess
seoDescription: Collect a limited edition print based on a ceramic artwork by Magdalena Suarez Frimkess. Homage for Jasper Johns combines two American icons as Minnie Mouse dances across the Star-Spangled Banner.
description:
Americana runs free in a limited edition print by Magdalena Suarez Frimkess.

At 95 years old, Magdalena continues to combine characters, symbols and objects with little concern for what they might mean. In Homage for Jasper Johns, two icons meet as Minnie Mouse dances across the Star-Spangled Banner. The artwork’s title nods to Jasper Johns and his painted renditions of the American flag, which Magdalena encountered after moving from Venezuela to America.

Printmakers at Make-Ready in London carefully transformed the original artwork, a handmade ceramic tile, into a limited edition print. Two layers of silkscreen varnish recreate its lustrous surface, while a subtle printed shadow creates the illusion of a three-dimensional object.

Thousands of tiny figures form the illusion of a crevice. On close inspection, the figures each have their own story, interacting with empathy and solidarity.

During a month-long residency at Make-Ready in London, Pejac reinterpreted the crevice on a blank canvas. His progress was documented, with each stage of the artwork corresponding with a unique print in a series of 1000. As a final flourish, one figure from each print is leafed in 24 carat gold leaf. In this figure, the artist hopes the viewer can see themselves shining amongst the crowd.

description:
Cool weather can’t mar a day at the beach in a surreal print by Wang Zhibo.

In 15º, Nationalistic Optimism by the Sea, an abstract figure relaxes on the sand. Behind them hangs a deep red curtain, and beyond it stand two poised poodles. By obscuring her subject Zhibo also obscures the emotional conditions of the seaside scene. Its title provides the only clue, albeit cryptic, as to what's going on.

The painting, now transformed into a silkscreen print with pearlescent highlights, was inspired by the culture shock Zhibo experienced after moving to Germany and seeing people frequent the beach whatever the weather. Observing this prompted her to reflect on how the shared experience of simple pleasures can disguise unresolved sociopolitical tensions.
